card.band: 8h. The levers are clear but each evaluation takes minutes; overfitting to the train families hurts on the hidden set. A frontier agent improves; a weaker model breaks correctness or overfits.
card.cheat: Wrong answers score zero because a SAT model is checked. Hidden families are not in /app, so tuning to the train set alone does not help.
card.grading: The solver is built and run on hidden instances from other families at a 10-60s cutoff, scored by PAR-2 and solved count. Reward is normalised between the baseline and the reference. UNSAT/SAT answers are checked (model verified; DRAT-free).
card.reference: Our tuned EasySAT. The paper reports PAR2 gains, for example 503 to 215 on ascon and 10,000 to 1,178 on register allocation, that guide the ceiling; Kissat is for context only.
card.task: /app ships EasySAT unmodified, as a small C++ solver with modular restart, reduce, rephase and bump heuristics, plus a train set of CNF instances (generated families and SAT-competition-style ones, licence of competition files not found, so regenerated families are used). The agent improves the solver over iterations and delivers the source.
card.title: CDCL heuristic tuning on EasySAT for unseen families

source_notes: Paper settings: timeout q:"is 5000s for each SAT instance", 12 datasets (7 from SC2023 families, 5 Picat), tests on 3 AMD EPYC 7763 servers: far too heavy, scale to 10-60 s cutoffs and instances EasySAT solves in seconds. OOD split: tune on some families (e.g. SC2023), hidden on others (Picat Zamkeller, KnightTour). Levers: restart policy, clause DB reduction, VSIDS/bump scheme, rephasing, plus data-structure/inprocessing work. Paper reports MiniSat beaten on 9 of 12 datasets, Kissat on 4. INFERRED: 100 instances x 30 s cutoff / 8 cores about 6-10 min per eval worst case. Single-source (paper); numbers read from PDF tables.
source_version: Baseline: EasySAT unmodified (9 modular heuristic functions: restart, restart condition(+update), reduce(+condition), rephase(+condition), bump var, bump var heuristic). -> Reference: AutoSAT (GPT-4o, budget B=60 LLM rewrites, greedy hill climber or (1+1) EA) and, for context, Kissat. Paper Table 2 PAR2 (solved): cryptography-ascon EasySAT 503 (20) -> 215 (20), Kissat 146 (20); register-allocation 10,000 (0) -> 1,178 (18), Kissat 8,554 (5); Zamkeller 3,668 (54) -> 2,053 (66).

Band.why: No dated public evidence of agents on this task; at most 3 without it.

Build.why: Reference tuning and eval harness take several days.

Fit.why: C++ CPU solver within 8 cores and 16 GB, no network needed.

Hor.why: 8 h with minutes per eval supports sustained iteration, but the scope may fit in fewer hours.

Lic.why: MIT for EasySAT; the regenerated families avoid the unclear competition-file licence.

Multi.why: Several levers and family buckets give partial credit, though the levers interact.

Real.why: Public MIT repo and a peer-reviewed paper with tables; the tuned solver itself is not public.

Ref.why: No public tuned reference; we must produce it, and its strength on the hidden split is unmeasured.

Seal.why: Hidden families are regenerated and absent from /app; the tuned reference is not in the paper's text.

Surf.why: Hidden CNF families with model checks give hundreds of instances, but the grader is still small compared with an executable oracle.

spike_plan.kill_if: Verdicts or timing are too noisy to rank changes (K4), or no lever beats noise on the held-out family, so the reference gap cannot be shown (K5/K8).
spike_plan.pass_if: Build succeeds, verdicts are deterministic, run-to-run PAR2 variance is under about 5%, and at least one lever gives a gain beyond noise on the held-out family.
steps: In a throwaway networked Linux container, clone shaowei-cai-group/EasySAT and build with g++ -O2; record build time and that it produces a binary.

Generate about 30 instances from two families: random 3-SAT near threshold and one structured family (e.g. a small pigeonhole or encoded scheduling set). Keep each solvable in 10-60 s by the baseline.
Write a grader: run the solver with a 30 s cutoff over 8 parallel jobs, check SAT models with an independent checker, and compute PAR2 and solved count.
Run the baseline twice to measure run-to-run PAR2 variance and check that SAT/UNSAT verdicts are identical across runs.
Change one lever (e.g. restart interval or clause-DB reduce schedule) and measure PAR2 on the same set plus a held-out family. Compare the gain against the run-to-run noise.
Time one full eval cycle to confirm it fits in minutes.

v1.summary: The seed's source, licence and paper results check out: EasySAT is MIT C++ and the paper's Table 2 reports the 503→215 and 10,000→1,178 figures at a 5000 s timeout, though the tuned code is not public and the JAIR version reports a different dataset count. The idea passes the gates on paper with no kill, but Ref (2) and timing noise at 10-60 s are open risks, so the spike must confirm that levers beat run-to-run noise on held-out families before building the reference.
